facts.raw_span: A man in his 70s presented with swelling of the manubrium
12 years after resection of a large left substernal thyroid lobe through a midline sternotomy approach
The swelling was slightly tender and had increased in size markedly over the month prior to presentation
Swelling noted over the manubrium, which was slightly tender
lytic lesion replacing the manubrium measuring 2.7 × 4.4 × 5.8 cm
residual right goiter
The posterior aspect is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein
Revealed follicular thyroid cells in the goiter and the manubrial lesion
Hematoxylin-eosin stained specimens showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae
previous substernal left hemithyroidectomy for benign goiter 12 years ago

contradict_spans: Hematoxylin-eosin stained specimens showing thyroid follicles infiltrating adjacent to bone trabeculae
concepts.why: The history of previous substernal goiter resection and the presence of residual goiter and follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion suggest a possible recurrence.
The posterior aspect of the lytic mass is in close proximity to the brachiocephalic artery and the left innominate vein, indicating potential mediastinal extension.

rationales.F05: Lytic lesion in the manubrium suggests aggressive behavior, more typical of metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma
rationales.F08: Follicular thyroid cells in the manubrial lesion support the diagnosis of metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma
rationales.F09: Infiltration of thyroid follicles into bone trabeculae is characteristic of metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma
